content:
Bug report: Content-Type parameters with quoted values are parsed incorrectly.

Fastify parses the parameters of a Content-Type header (`type/subtype; name=value; ...`)
by splitting on `;`. That breaks as soon as a parameter value is a quoted string that
contains a `;`. For example, with

    multipart/mixed; boundary="part;one"; charset=utf-8

the parsed `boundary` is cut off at the `;` instead of being `part;one`. Worse, text
inside a quoted value can be mistaken for parameters of its own: for

    text/plain; title="lang=en; charset=latin1"

Fastify reports a `charset` parameter of `latin1`, although the header declares no
charset at all; `latin1` is just part of the `title` value.

Expected behavior: parameter values are parsed as the HTTP specification (RFC 9110)
defines them, token or quoted-string. In particular:

- A `;` inside a quoted parameter value is part of that value, and the parameters that
  follow the quoted value are still parsed correctly.
- Nothing inside a quoted value is ever treated as a separate parameter.

Work within this local repository and the context you have been given. Do not
look up this project or its history online.

Verify your work before you finish: add or update automated tests that cover
the change, run them together with the existing tests for the code you touched,
and make sure they pass.

content:
Quoted parameter values in `Content-Type` are now parsed per RFC 9110, and the new and existing content-type tests pass (32 tests, 0 failures) with lint clean.

- **Fix** (`lib/content-type.js`): the `;`-splitting regex is replaced with a small scanner. A quoted value now runs to its closing quote, so `;` and `=` inside it stay part of the value, and later parameters still parse. `\` escapes inside quoted values are unescaped.
- **Your two examples:**
  - `boundary="part;one"; charset=utf-8` gives `boundary` = `part;one` and `charset` = `utf-8`.
  - `title="lang=en; charset=latin1"` gives only `title`, with no `charset`.
- **Invalid quoted values:**
  - An unterminated quote, or text after the closing quote (`a="x"y`), marks that parameter `invalid quoted string`, as before.
  - For an unterminated quote, everything after it is consumed as part of that value, so later parameters are dropped rather than parsed.
- **Tests:** I added a "ContentType quoted parameter values" suite to `test/content-type.test.js`. It covers the two reported cases, escaped quotes and backslashes, and the invalid forms.
